newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Italy failed to fully implement VAT directive.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Italy failed to fully implement VAT directive.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Wednesday Italy failed to implement fully Community tax laws by continuing to tax the supply of goods characterized as exempt under the Sixth VAT directive.

Although Italy stipulated certain goods listed in the directive are not exempt under Italian tax law, it argued that a taxable person who buys goods for an exempt activity normally acquires them for personal use, and any subsequent supply of those goods is hypothetical, or incurs a very small tax.

The court said "even if the VAT due in the event of double taxation would in fact be insignificant...that cannot absolve Italy from properly implementing Community law whose very purpose is to avoid double taxation contrary to the prinicple of fiscal neutrality inherent in the common system of value added tax."
Commission of the European Communities, applicant

application for a declaration that, by enacting and maintaining in force legislation which does not exempt from value added tax supplies of goods used wholly for an exempted activity or in any event excluded from the right of deduction, the Italian Republic has failed to fulfil its obligations under article 13(B) of the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

1. Declares that, by enacting and maintaining in force legislation which does not exempt from value added tax supplies of goods used wholly for an exempted activity or in any event excluded from the right of deduction, the Italian Republic has failed to fulfil its obligations under article 13(B) of the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment;
2. Orders the parties to bear their own costs.
